scope: Protocol-only comparison of the two authorized files; no tooling, canonical summary, bank, reader or grading execution reviewed.

checks.criterion: Model chooses governing procedure and facts; tools only perform mechanical operations
checks.finding: The new MODEL CHOICE paragraph requires reading and understanding the question and source before choosing procedure, sections and facts. It forbids automated question-to-section matching, sentence ranking, keyword/phrase routing and code-generated unsupported fallbacks. Generic heading indexing, copying model-selected exact slices, JSON serialization and literal checks remain allowed.

checks.criterion: Lookup failure does not establish missing source content
checks.finding: A failed string lookup or empty search hit is expressly a locator error requiring rereading/correction. It cannot automatically produce an unsupported answer. This does not require claiming support when the source genuinely lacks the fact.

checks.criterion: Unsupported clauses receive a substantive reread while honest absence remains allowed
checks.finding: Before retaining an unsupported clause, the reader must reread that entry’s complete attachments and relevant definitions, conditions and referenced procedures in the same frozen summary, looking for requested meaning rather than wording. An answering operative rule requires repair; genuine absence permits a precise unsupported statement identifying the remaining unknown and checked contexts. The protocol expressly rejects guessing or assuming all answers must be supported.

checks.criterion: Per-request self-check compares actual rule context and requested result
checks.finding: For each individual request, the self-check records the question’s and quote’s governing procedure/condition, actor and requested outcome/destination. Neighboring or differently conditioned rules cannot stand in for the requested rule. Referenced sections must be checked for their actual restrictions/destinations. Confidence and format labels are expressly not the semantic check.

checks.criterion: fact_source_section identifies a source location, not source text
checks.finding: The quoted-fact instruction explicitly requires the bare computed H-number ID string and forbids a full source section, heading title or path. This locates a declared quote without supplying a factual answer. Unsupported source absence remains separately allowed; the protocol does not require inventing a supporting section.

checks.criterion: No game facts, failed IDs, expected answers or key hints
checks.finding: The added rules are generic semantic-selection and review instructions. Neither protocol introduces game-specific mechanics, factual answers, actual question/failed IDs, keys or reader results. H-number is a generic source-location format, not a question answer.

checks.criterion: Identical instructions and fresh full-bank blindness preserved
checks.finding: The opening input restrictions and complete initial delivery are unchanged. Both readers receive the identical shared protocol except role/path; every summary line, complete question object and actual final ID must be delivered, with all ordered IDs retained. This checks the template requirement rather than unseen dispatches.

checks.criterion: Substantive grading and exact source requirements are not weakened
checks.finding: The same-entry substantive-content policy, ordinary exact-fact/minimal-case policy, full source-section attachments, schema and first-draft preservation are byte-identical paragraphs to v5. Literal/format success does not replace semantic requested-fact coverage; other questions/readers cannot supply omissions. New checks strengthen relevance and honest abstention without altering asked facts or keys.

Definitions, procedural references, phase transitions and exceptions must be followed within the frozen summary when needed. The new instructions do not authorize source rules, keys, outside knowledge, earlier outputs or additional files.

conclusion: The new rules require the model to select and verify actual governing facts, restrict code to mechanical treatment of model-selected data, and review every abstention in its own source context. They remain generic/blind and preserve full-bank substantive grading.
